items.action: Update WordPress Core to 7.1.4 or later immediately, and check sites that recently ran full-package upgrades for signs of compromise.
items.details: The flaw is a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in full-package core upgrades, where predictable, web-accessible staging paths could let an unauthenticated attacker execute code on the server during the upgrade window. WordPress 7.1.4 addresses it.
items.summary: CISA has added WordPress Core vulnerability CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after evidence of active exploitation, with a November 6 remediation deadline for federal civilian agencies.
items.title: CISA adds exploited WordPress Core flaw to KEV; patch by Nov 6

items.action: Apply the November 2026 Android security patch (2026-11-01 level or later) as soon as your manufacturer ships it, and prioritise devices still on older patch levels.
items.details: Devices receive the fix through security patch level 2026-11-01 or later, depending on manufacturer and carrier. The bulletin includes 23 vulnerabilities rated Critical, including flaws in the System component and modem code.
items.summary: Google's November 2026 Android security bulletin fixes 216 vulnerabilities, including critical flaw CVE-2026-58868, a heap buffer overflow in FrameDecoder that could allow remote code execution with no user interaction on Android 14 through 17.
items.title: Google's November Android bulletin fixes critical remote-code flaw

items.action: Apply Barracuda's November 2 firmware patches and restrict appliance administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks only.
items.details: Barracuda has not reported exploitation of either flaw. Exploitation requires access to the appliance's administrative interface, so internet-exposed admin interfaces are the priority. ESG patches are BNSF-40425 (9.4.017+) and BNSF-40430 (earlier versions).
items.summary: Barracuda has patched CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3), and CVE-2026-111560, a command-injection flaw across six products (CVSS 8.6), which combined could give root access to a device.
items.title: Barracuda patches two flaws chainable to root on security appliances

items.action: Law and insurance firms should review exposed credentials and third-party access, and watch for client data appearing in extortion channels.
items.details: The claimed haul includes 4,477 workers' compensation defence case files, 6,461 DICOM medical imaging files, and 28,410 medical explanations of benefits containing personal information and diagnoses. This is a threat-actor claim, not yet independently confirmed by the firm.
items.summary: The Rhysida ransomware group has claimed the law firm Juge, Napolitano, Ruli, Putfark & Pittman (WC Defense), claiming to have exfiltrated about 3.2 TB of data totalling 2,383,324 files.
items.title: Rhysida claims 3.2 TB theft from Louisiana law firm WC Defense

items.action: Monitor for corroboration and, if you share data with the named supply chain, verify whether any of your records are in scope.
items.details: The group claims the data spans three regions and includes contacts, shipment records, invoices and distributor loyalty profiles. The claim is unverified and the group is newly discovered, so treat it as an emerging allegation, not a confirmed breach.
items.summary: A newly surfaced ransomware group calling itself Whitearmor listed Unilever on its leak site on November 4, claiming 79 GB of exfiltrated data across 1.8 million files and demanding $15 million in Bitcoin.
items.title: New group Whitearmor claims Unilever breach, demands $15M

items.action: Nonprofits holding donor and beneficiary data should rotate exposed credentials and review financial-system access after any such claim.
items.details: The claim, reported November 4, also notes infostealer-linked credential exposure for the organisation. No ransom demand, attack vector or recovery status has been reported.
items.summary: The Dark Project ransomware group claims to have exfiltrated more than 130 GB of data from the Food Bank of Central Louisiana, including banking and financial information and personal data of employees and clients.
items.title: Dark Project claims 130 GB theft from Food Bank of Central Louisiana

items.action: BFSI entities should harden payment and disbursement APIs, retire dormant interfaces, enforce transaction limits and beneficiary verification, and report incidents to CERT-In promptly.
items.details: The November 4 advisory, an update to the October 9 advisory, says the actor uses publicly available AI tools such as ARTEX, PentAGI and Cairn, re-targets entities that already remediated, and times attacks for holidays and low-monitoring windows. It urges heightened 24x7 monitoring and staffing during low-coverage periods.
items.summary: CERT-In has issued critical advisory CIAD-2026-0058 naming 'Crafty Falcon', an AI-assisted threat actor exploiting payment and disbursement APIs for unauthorised fund transfers at machine speed across banks, NBFCs and fintechs.
items.title: CERT-In warns of AI-driven 'Crafty Falcon' attacks on BFSI payment APIs

items.action: Corporate treasury teams should review API-based payment controls, dual authorisation and anomaly alerts on high-value RTGS flows.
items.details: The company says the transactions went through Yes Bank's payment API, that it activated incident response, moved to freeze beneficiary accounts, and reported the matter to the Cyber Crime Cell, RBI and CERT-In, appointing an independent investigating agency. Core operations and customer data are stated to be unaffected.
items.summary: SG Finserve disclosed on November 3 that 15 unauthorised RTGS and electronic banking transactions totalling ₹5.10 crore were executed from two of its Yes Bank current accounts without its knowledge or authorisation.
items.title: SG Finserve discloses ₹5.10 crore unauthorised RTGS fraud via Yes Bank API

items.action: Treat the listing as a watch item: check for any exposure linked to the named organisation rather than assuming a confirmed compromise.
items.details: No intrusion details, stolen-data volume, ransom demand or operational impact were reported with the listing. Akira also listed a manufacturing firm, Erowa, the same day.
items.summary: Threat-intelligence monitoring reports that the Akira ransomware group listed Krishnan, categorised under India's finance sector, as a victim on November 4 — a threat-actor claim that has not been independently confirmed as a breach.
items.title: Akira claims Indian finance firm Krishnan among new victims (unverified)
